description:
About Kiddom

Kiddom is transforming K–12 education by bringing high-quality curriculum, instructional tools, and student analytics together in one coherent system. We are building Learning Intelligence Technology (LIT), a new category that gives educators the infrastructure to plan, teach, assess, and respond to student needs. With Kiddom, educators spend less time managing administrative burden and more time delivering meaningful student instruction. Kiddom helps schools and districts deliver more equitable, effective, and adaptive learning experiences.

Role overview

Kiddom is building a bench of contract Instructional Design Consultants who bring subject expertise and judgment to specific, scoped curriculum projects. You'll partner with one of our Curriculum Product Managers (CPMs), who owns a program end to end, and take on defined work: authoring and revising lessons and assessments, building digital and print-ready materials, and reviewing content for quality and standards alignment.

This isn't a generic production role. AI and internal tools now handle much of the assembly; we need people who can decide what good looks like, catch what the tools get wrong, and stand behind the final product. Consultants are matched to work by expertise, and pay reflects the complexity of the task, not a single flat rate.

What you'll do

Work is assigned project by project. Depending on your tier and expertise, you may:

  • Author and revise lessons, tasks, assessment items, teacher notes and supplemental materials aligned to state and national standards

  • Build and edit interactive question types and lesson content in Kiddom's authoring tools

  • Design and update lesson slide decks and other teacher- and student-facing resources for digital and print

  • Review AI-assisted and contractor-produced content for accuracy, instructional intent and standards alignment, and resolve QA tickets

  • Localize content for state adoptions (e.g., Florida, Georgia, Texas, North Carolina), including state-specific standards, review criteria and language requirements

  • For senior engagements: architect scope and sequence, map prerequisites and skills, or advise on program design

  • Track hours against the correct project code, meet agreed deadlines, and flag blockers early to your CPM

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years of K-12 classroom teaching in your subject area

  • 1–3+ years of instructional design or curriculum writing experience

  • Deep familiarity with relevant standards (Common Core, NGSS, state-specific frameworks)

  • A point of view: you can make and defend content decisions, not just execute a spec

  • Comfort reviewing and correcting AI-generated content with a critical eye

  • Strong detail orientation, clear communication, and a track record of hitting deadlines on your own

  • Experience with Google Slides/PowerPoint and digital lesson delivery tools (e.g., Nearpod, Pear Deck) is a plus

  • State adoption experience (writing to review criteria, TCOs, correlations) is a strong plus

Specialty tracks

Below is the Track and Experience we value:

Math - Grades 6–12 teaching (high school preferred); K–5 conceptual and manipulative-based instruction; Illustrative Mathematics

Science - Middle and high school; OpenSciEd, OpenStax; NGSS; simulations such as PhET or Labster

ELA - EL Education curriculum; domain expertise in key adoption states

ELD / MLL - English language development design and multilingual-learner supports

Engagement model and compensation

This is a remote, hourly contract role. Rates are tied to the type of work, not to a title, so one consultant may work across tiers on different projects. General curriculum work and content QA (most project tasks are here) start at $31/hr.

  • Each CPM keeps a small dedicated pool of consultants, so strong performers get steady, recurring work

  • Contracts run up to 12 months

  • Final rates depend on experience, expertise and the scope of each project

What we offer

  • Full time permanent employees are eligible for the following benefits from their first day of employment:

  • Competitive salary

  • Meaningful equity

  • Health insurance benefits: medical (various PPO/HMO/HSA plans), dental, vision, disability and life insurance

  • 401k plan

  • One Medical membership (in participating locations)

  • Flexible vacation time policy (subject to internal approval). Average use 4 weeks off per year.

  • 10 paid sick days per year (pro rated depending on start date)

  • Paid holidays

  • Paid bereavement leave

  • Paid family leave after birth/adoption. Minimum of 16 paid weeks for birthing parents, 10 weeks for caretaker parents. Meant to supplement benefits offered by State.

  • Commuter and FSA plans


Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Kiddom is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, color, gender, sexual orientation, transgender status, national origin, citizenship status, uniform service member status, pregnancy, age, genetic information, disability, or any other protected status in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.
